claims.statement: A requirement walks nine micro-states — 立项, 计划中, 计划门禁, 待开发, 开发中, 交付受理, 验收门禁, 集成, done — and the ninth is terminal.
All three push-back paths (`proposal.reject`, `gate.reject`, `integration.reject`) land on 待开发 with `plan_ok` kept, `job` cleared and the lane released — R6 in one sentence.

The delivery-acceptance stage is deliberately asymmetric: a plan proposal goes straight from its gate to 待开发, while a development delivery gets one extra serial review stage at the coordination layer.
Submitting a development delivery does not release the lane (R7); only rejection or confirmation does, which keeps the worktree tied to the requirement until the outcome is known.
Accepting a delivery re-checks freshness — `gate_rev` must equal `rev` — so an amended requirement cannot be approved against a stale gate revision.
`blocked` (conflict or `needs_amend`) is an overlay that `req_display()` lays over `req_phase()`, never a tenth micro-state.
The stage names on this page match `scenes.json`'s `reqStage` ordering exactly, so the read-plan and the state machine never disagree about what stage a requirement is in.
